Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

# Conservative Party Manifesto 2024: Summary

## Economic Foundation and Vision

The Conservative Party presents this manifesto on a platform of restored economic stability following COVID-19 and the Ukraine crisis. They highlight falling inflation, rising real wages, and returning growth as evidence their economic plan is working. The party pledges to maintain fiscal discipline while cutting taxes, with debt and borrowing targets remaining core commitments.

## Key Tax Proposals

The Conservatives promise significant tax cuts for workers, including halving employee National Insurance from 12% to 6% by April 2027, saving average workers £1,350 annually. They plan to completely abolish self-employed National Insurance by Parliament's end. For pensioners, the new "Triple Lock Plus" guarantees both the State Pension and pensioner tax-free allowance rise with the highest of inflation, earnings, or 2.5%. Child Benefit reforms will shift to household-based assessment, with benefits retained until combined income reaches £120,000.

## Immigration and Border Security

Immigration control features prominently, with promises to introduce a legal, binding cap on migration set annually by Parliament. The party commits to continuing Rwanda deportation flights, ending illegal migration, and working internationally to reform asylum treaties. Legal migration thresholds have already been raised, with the Skilled Worker visa salary requirement increased to £38,700.

## Defence and National Security

Defence spending will increase to 2.5% of GDP by 2030, representing the largest sustained increase since the Cold War. The party commits to supporting Ukraine, maintaining the nuclear deterrent, and investing in new military capabilities including munitions production and defence technology. A National Defence and Resilience Plan will be developed.

## NHS and Healthcare

NHS spending will increase above inflation annually, with commitments to recruit 92,000 more nurses and 28,000 more doctors. Plans include expanding Pharmacy First services, building 250 GP surgeries, and establishing 50 additional Community Diagnostic Centres. Mental health receives attention with promises to expand school support teams and talking therapies.

## Housing

The party targets 1.6 million new homes, abolishing EU nutrient neutrality rules to unlock 100,000 homes immediately. Stamp Duty abolition for first-time buyers on properties up to £425,000 will be made permanent, alongside a new Help to Buy scheme. Green Belt protections will remain while brownfield development is prioritised.

## Young People and Education

A mandatory National Service programme for 18-year-olds offers choices between military placement or civic volunteering. Education commitments include 100,000 new apprenticeships funded by closing poor-performing university courses, and introducing the Advanced British Standard for 16-19 education. Mobile phone bans in schools will become statutory.

## Energy and Environment

The party maintains commitment to net zero by 2050 while promising a "pragmatic" approach, guaranteeing no new green levies and annual oil and gas licensing rounds. Nuclear expansion includes approving two Small Modular Reactor fleets within 100 days. They commit to trebling offshore wind capacity while protecting agricultural land from solar farms.

## Community and Local Government

Transport investment of £36 billion from HS2 savings will fund local roads, rail, and buses, including £8.3 billion for pothole repairs. The "Backing Drivers Bill" will stop road pricing, reverse London's ULEZ expansion, and require local referendums for new 20mph zones. Towns will receive £20 million endowment funds for local improvements.
